chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man asked my father about the wars of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the questioner was from our lovers. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him:

Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with five swords, three of which are unsheathed and will not be sheathed until 'War lays down its burdens.' And War will not lay down its burdens until the sun rises from its west. When the sun rises from its west, all people will believe on that day, so on that day 'Not will be the faith of a soul which had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good.'
And one of them is a sheathed sword, and one is a contained sword; its drawing is for others, and its ruling is for us.

As for the three unsheathed swords, the first is against the polytheists of the Arabs. Allah said: 'Slay the idolaters wherever you find them, and take them, and besiege them, and lie in wait for them in every ambuscade.' If they repent, meaning if they believe, 'and establish prayer and give alms-tax, then they are your brothers in religion.' These are accepted from them only killing or entering Islam, so their wealth and descendants are taken as booty as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took. For he took, forgave, and accepted ransom.

The second sword is against the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma). Allah said: 'And speak to people good words,' which was revealed regarding the People of the Covenant. Then it was abrogated by His saying: 'Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day and who do not consider prohibited what Allah and His Messenger have prohibited and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.'

Whoever of them is in the House of Islam, accepted from him is only the jizyah or killing, and their wealth is booty (fa') and their descendants are taken as captives. When they accept the jizyah, it becomes prohibited for us to take their captives and wealth, and marriage with them becomes permissible for us. And whoever of them is in the House of War, their captivity is permissible for us, but marriage with them is not permissible, and accepted from them is only the jizyah or killing.

The third sword is a sword against the polytheists of the Ajam, meaning the Turks, Khazar, and Daylam. Allah said in the beginning of the Surah where He mentions those who disbelieved and recounts their story: 'Then [take] the necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter among them, then bind the bonds firmly.' Meaning captivity. 'Or [accept] ransom.' Meaning exchange between them and the people of Islam. These will be accepted from them only killing or entering Islam, and marriage with them is not permissible for us as long as they are in the House of War.

As for the sheathed sword, it is the sword of the People of Revolt and Interpretation. Allah said: 'And if two parties of the believers fight, then make settlement between the two' until His saying: 'until they return to the command of Allah.' When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, from among you is one who will fight after me based on interpretation just as I fought based on revelation.'
So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: Who is he? He said: 'He is the Sandal-Mender,' meaning the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).

And 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: I fought with this banner with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) three times, so this is the fourth. By Allah, if they struck us until we reached the palm shoots of Hajjar, we would know that we are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood.

And the conduct regarding them from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was as it was from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the people of Mecca on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, for he did not take their descendants as captives. And he said: 'Whoever closes his door or throws down his weapon or enters the house of Abu Sufyan, he is safe.'

And thus the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding them: 'Do not take their descendants as captives, do not finish off the wounded, do not pursue the fleeing, and whoever closes his door or throws down his weapon, he is safe.'
As for the contained sword, it is the sword by which qisas (retaliation) is established. Allah said: 'Life for life' [the verse]. Its drawing is for the heirs of the slain, and its ruling is for us.

These are the swords with which Allah sent His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Whoever denies them or denies one of them or something of their conduct and rulings has disbelieved in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَغْيِ: People of Revolt (those who rebel against the Imam)
key_terms.سَبْيٌ: Captivity/taking of people as prisoners of war

ai.seo_question: What are the five categories of warfare and their corresponding legal rulings in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the five distinct categories of warfare and legal authority established by the Prophet, with a specific Shia emphasis on the 'sheathed sword' of *Ahl al-Bagh* (People of Revolt) being uniquely linked to Imam Ali through the 'Slipper Bearer' prophecy. It systematically differentiates the rules of captivity, ransom, and marriage for Arab polytheists, People of the Book, and non-Arab polytheists, while affirming that the sword of *Qisas* (retaliation) remains under the jurisdiction of the Imam. The text concludes that denial of any of these swords or their specific rulings constitutes disbelief in the revelation given to Muhammad.
